pr.title: Dont ICE when computing coverage of synthetic async closure body
pr.description:
I'm not totally certain if this is *right*, but at least it doesn't ICE.

The issue is that we end up generating two MIR bodies for each async closure, since the `FnOnce` and `Fn`/`FnMut` implementations have different borrowing behavior of their captured variables. They should ideally both contribute to the coverage, since those MIR bodies are (*to the user*) the same code and should have no behavioral differences.

This PR at least suppresses the ICEs, and then I guess worst case we can fix this the right way later.

r? Zalathar or re-roll

Fixes #131190
pr.author: compiler-errors

processing.reason: The PR describes a compiler-internal ICE, not a user-code miscompilation. The historically wrong transformation is InstrumentCoverage calling `extract_hir_info`/`coverage_attr_on` on a synthetic async-closure MIR body def_id that has no HIR entry; that def_id lookup indexes out of bounds and aborts compilation. The corrected behavior redirects HIR extraction to the synthetic body's `local_parent` and propagates `coverage_attr_on` to the by-move coroutine body. There is no source-grounded pair of ordinary Rust functions with identical inputs whose successful executions produce different numeric/boolean/character values: the incorrect revision either fails to compile the test crate (ICE) or, if modeled as an index, panics rather than returning a different value. Manufacturing an unrelated value-changing rewrite would not encode the historical transformation, so no valid counterexample pair can be validated.

evidence: Dont ICE when computing coverage of synthetic async closure body
The issue is that we end up generating two MIR bodies for each async closure, since the `FnOnce` and `Fn`/`FnMut` implementations have different borrowing behavior of their captured variables.
This PR at least suppresses the ICEs, and then I guess worst case we can fix this the right way later.

analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior was to run coverage HIR extraction directly on each synthetic MIR body def_id. For async closures, two MIR bodies are generated (different borrowing behavior for `FnOnce` vs `Fn`/`FnMut`), producing synthetic def_ids such as `main::{closure#0}::{closure#0}::{closure#1}` that are not present in the HIR map. Looking up `local_def_id_to_hir_id`/`hir_node_by_def_id` for such a def_id panicked with an index-out-of-bounds, and `coverage_attr_on` was not inherited by the by-move body, so the attribute source was also inconsistent. This is a compiler-internal transformation bug, not a miscompilation of user code: the wrong transformation is treating a synthetic MIR body as if it were an ordinary HIR-backed body.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs compiled with `-Cinstrument-coverage` that contain async closures (feature `async_closure`), especially `async move` closures passed to an `async FnOnce` bound and capturing/dropping values, so that the coroutine by-move body is synthesized. The problematic def_ids are synthetic MIR body def_ids whose HIR owner is the enclosing closure/function; ordinary HIR-backed functions are unaffected.
analysis.originalLogic: InstrumentCoverage's `extract_hir_info` assumed every def_id being instrumented had a corresponding HIR node and body: it called `tcx.hir_node_by_def_id(def_id)` and then `hir_node.body_id().expect("HIR node is a function with body")`. Separately, the by-move coroutine body builder inherited various attributes from the by-ref coroutine (`codegen_fn_attrs`, `constness`, `coroutine_kind`, `def_ident_span`, etc.) but did not inherit `coverage_attr_on`. Thus coverage eligibility/attribute lookup and HIR extraction were performed per raw MIR def_id, including synthetic MIR bodies.
pitfalls: Do not assume every MIR body def_id has a HIR node or HIR body: synthetic MIR bodies (async closure by-move bodies) need their HIR owner resolved via `local_parent`.
The presence of a coverage attribute must be propagated when constructing a synthetic/by-move coroutine body; otherwise coverage decisions for the two async-closure bodies can diverge.

Suppressing the ICE is not the same as fully correct coverage: the PR itself says `I'm not totally certain if this is *right*` and `This PR at least suppresses the ICEs`, so do not claim the ideal two-body coverage accounting was achieved.
The issue is specifically about querying HIR (`local_def_id_to_hir_id`) for a synthetic def_id; other queries may legitimately be valid for such def_ids, so do not over-generalize the workaround.
Do not infer the wrong rewrite from the golden `.cov-map`/`.coverage` expectations alone; those are regression expectations for the corrected compiler.
preconditions: The crate uses the unstable `async_closure` feature and defines an async closure (e.g. `async || {}` or `async move |a| {}`).
The async closure causes separate/synthetic MIR bodies to be generated for its `FnOnce` and `Fn`/`FnMut` implementations, including a by-move body.
The synthetic body's def_id is not a HIR-backed body, so `tcx.local_parent(def_id)` (not the synthetic def_id itself) owns the real HIR body.
analysis.summary: Coverage instrumentation ICEs on synthetic MIR bodies of async closures because it queries HIR for a def_id that has no HIR node; the fix redirects HIR extraction to the synthetic body's local parent and propagates the coverage attribute to the by-move coroutine body.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a compile/run UI-style coverage test (`tests/coverage/async_closure.rs`) using `#![feature(async_closure)]`, edition 2021, an async executor aux-build, an `async fn call_once(f: impl async FnOnce())`, and both `block_on(async_closure())` and `block_on(call_once(async_closure))`; keep the corresponding `.coverage` and `.cov-map` golden expectations. Ensure the regression covers the by-move/synthetic-body path, e.g. an `async move` closure with a captured/dropped argument as in the removed crash test. Delete the `known-bug` crash test only when the compiler no longer ICEs. This was verified as a test expectation change, not by building/running the compiler in this analysis.
analysis.trigger: Coverage instrumentation reaches a synthetic MIR body (the by-move/`FnOnce` body of an async closure) whose def_id has no HIR entry. Both the direct `extract_hir_info` call on that synthetic def_id and the missing inherited `coverage_attr_on` participate.
